issues.passage: Everyone followed the same idiosyncratic checklist issued by headquarters.
issues.why: Idiosyncratic commonly describes an institution's own quirky process (e.g. "the agency's idiosyncratic checklist"), so a HQ checklist everyone follows can still read as valid "highly distinctive" usage. wrongPassages[1] has the same problem: an enforced house format can reasonably be called idiosyncratic. Only wrongPassages[2] clearly contradicts the definition.

fix.correctPassage: Her idiosyncratic color code made the spreadsheet unreadable to anyone else on the team.
wrongPassages: The mandatory form used an idiosyncratic layout copied verbatim from every other agency's template.
Her idiosyncratic method was simply the standard procedure already printed in every textbook.
Regulators praised the idiosyncratic protocol for eliminating personal variation across every lab.

issues.passage: The style guide enforced one idiosyncratic format so that all reports looked identical.
issues.why: A distinctive house style enforced so all reports match can still be described as idiosyncratic; "identical" only means internal uniformity, not that the format is ordinary or non-distinctive. Same fix set as wrongPassages[0].
